0.17.3 - - Sonos players now initialize through a queue, at most 3 at a time, instead of all at once. This reduces load and connection storms when the hub reboots or the app is saved.
- After a hub reboot, the app waits about 60 seconds for the hub to settle before it starts player initialization. A burst of child WebSocket requests at startup is also treated as a reboot and held for the same settling period.
- A player that fails to initialize after a reboot is retried once at the back of the queue. A player that still fails is deferred and retried hourly.
- Stuck initializations are timed out and cleaned up. A child that doesn't acknowledge the start is dropped after 2 seconds, and any initialization is dropped after 90 seconds overall.
- Stale commands are purged on initialization. A player TTS request created before a player's initialization is ignored instead of being replayed afterward.
- The Sonos event bridge is replaced with direct callbacks between players and the app. Initialization callbacks are honored and leftover bridge state is cleared. Player state updates and player requests, including active-stream TTS decisions, now flow through these callbacks.
- Fixed a missing audio clip queue start time, which is now preserved.
- Diagnostic messages previously logged at Trace (discovery, announcement routing, subscriptions, update notices, and similar) now log at Debug, so they show at the Debug log level.
- Discovery of secondary Sonos speakers is now logged at Info.
- Raw mDNS discovery payloads are omitted at Debug and included only at Trace.
- Announcement and TTS diagnostics are improved. Request logs now include the age of group commands and player requests plus correlation and request IDs. Failures to send a TTS response are logged as warnings.
0.16.2 - - Added **Stop Announcement** and **Stop High Priority Announcement** commands on Sonos player devices. They cancel the currently playing announcement only if its priority matches the command. A stop is skipped if Sonos hasn't yet reported the clip's ID.
- Improved announcement queue timing. The next queued announcement now starts at millisecond precision, with no extra one-second delay, after playback finishes, topology restoration completes, or the queue is released.
- Made Sonos WebSocket commands more reliable. Commands are tracked until Sonos acknowledges them, expire after 60 seconds, and the outbound queue is capped at 128 entries. Unacknowledged commands that are safe to repeat are replayed after a reconnect, once subscriptions are re-established.
- Reduced duplicate and stale replays. Newer playback, volume, mute and replace-media intents supersede older queued ones, and queued play-mode changes are merged. Group create and modify commands wait for a fresh groups snapshot, and replay is skipped if the groups already match.
- Avoided repeating announcements and transport commands. Unacknowledged announcement clips and transport commands are not auto-replayed. If Sonos acknowledges a transport command but playback status doesn't confirm it, the command is not resent.
- Stereo-pair announcements: the secondary (right-channel) player tracks audioClip acknowledgements, reconnects if its socket goes silent, and never replays a paired clip.
- Added an optional **Enable track position updates** setting (off by default) on Player and Group devices. It exposes `trackPosition` and `trackPositionUpdated` attributes. Turning the setting off resets both to 0.
- Reduced hub load from state updates. Player, group, alarm and battery state changes are now batched and coalesced. Unchanged values are skipped, and failed deliveries are retained and retried instead of dropped. Group state delivery no longer gives up after a fixed number of retries.
- Alarm Manager, Alarm Switch, group and player devices now send requests to the app through device events instead of direct app calls, making them more robust. Group commands are retried until acknowledged and are recovered after a hub restart or driver update.
- Improved diagnostics. Sonos WebSocket errors and player exceptions now include more detail, such as the exception class and stack trace. Group command and active-stream announcement handling now log more detail at trace level.
- Hardened audio clip callback parsing against malformed responses.
- Player devices stay in sync with the app's announcement audioClip policy and active-player roster.
0.15.10 - - **Alarm management (opt-in):** Two new options in the Alarm Management section.
  - A household-level Sonos Alarm Manager device.
  - One switch device per Sonos alarm. Each switch shows the alarm's time, volume, recurrence, room, duration, source, play mode and grouped-rooms setting.
  - You can enable, disable, change, create and delete alarms over the local Sonos interface.
  - You can set an alarm's source from your favorites or playlists.
  - Alarm switches refresh every 15 minutes.
  - Each option takes effect as soon as it is toggled.
  - The alarm manager has a TTS voice cache.
- **Queue and sleep timer controls:** New Sonos queue and sleep timer controls, with updated documentation. The queue display shows each entry's position (for example, "# 3 — Artist") above the album art. Entries with no artist show only the position number.
- **TTS no longer interrupts playback:**
  - New "Use a temporary stream holder" option, on by default. While standard-stream TTS plays, an idle speaker can briefly hold the active Sonos stream. The stream is then handed back to the original speaker, and the player's previous mute state is restored.
  - If no suitable idle speaker is available, or the option is off, announcements use synchronized audio clips so playback continues.
  - AirPlay streams are never handed to a holder and always use audio clips.
- **TTS chime and volume controls:**
  - New "Queue chime separately from TTS for better sync" option (off by default). It may add a slight delay between the chime and the start of TTS.
  - New "Suppress chime on successive TTS messages" option (off by default). Queued TTS messages that follow another TTS announcement start without an extra chime.
  - Optional Sonos playback volume handling is fixed.
- **Audio clip reliability:** The original topology and playback are restored and verified more reliably after announcements. Paired audio clips are now coordinated.
- **Refreshed new UI:**
  - Speakers and groups appear in card layouts with toolbars.
  - Discovery has a status indicator and a button.
  - Mobile layouts are available for speakers and groups.
  - The group editor has a redesigned form with a follower checklist. Editor and muted-progress display issues are fixed.
  - Logging and announcement settings are consolidated.
  - The old-UI toggle remains under Interface Settings.
- **Update notices:**
  - New-UI update notices use the card style with native buttons and restored styling.
  - Dismissing a Sonos update notice now works correctly.
- **More reliable group and favorite operations:**
  - Group operations are handled more robustly.
  - Sonos Favorite playback confirmation is hardened and its operation timeouts are improved.
  - Favorites are accepted when the topology is coordinator-only.
  - Post-Favorite topology selection is improved.
- **Subscription reliability:** Stale UPnP subscription ID replacement is handled correctly.
- **Packaging:** The Sonos Advanced package includes the Sonos alarm, queue and component drivers.
- **Quieter logs:** A selected speaker that is missing from Sonos discovery (offline, or not a Sonos player) is logged at info level instead of as a warning.
- **Release notes:** Release notes are generated with Copilot, and cumulative notes are improved.
0.14.1 Set TTS modes to "always non-interrupting"
0.14.0 Adds configurable, resilient Sonos group announcements with safer topology handling, offline TTS queue retention, and improved WebSocket and UPnP subscription recovery.
0.13.3 Add missing import
0.13.2 Add playTrackAndRestore(uri, volume) and playTrackAndResume(uri, volume)
0.13.1 Updated the Group driver to support the player’s speech and text entry points. It now declares AudioNotification and implements playText, playTextAndRestore, playTextAndResume, speak, and speakNoRestore. Volume inputs accept common numeric and string types.
0.13.0 Added async maintenance and discovery, serialized Sonos transport and UPnP handling, Line-In selection, and active-player cleanup; fixed topology, mute, balance, crossfade, announcement volume, priority playback, and update-state issues.
0.12.1 Added queued group command handling, improved coordinator and membership checks, and refined volume, mute, playback state, and topology updates.
0.12.0 ### Sonos Advanced Controller 0.11.12  - Improved reliability when several Sonos commands happen close together. - Playback commands now wait for speakers to finish grouping, helping prevent playback from interrupting group changes. - Improved recovery when Sonos responds slowly or misses a command. - Made playback status and audio notifications more reliable.
0.11.11 Use Hubitat theme CSS variables for Sonos speaker and group tables, including backgrounds, borders, text colors, secondary details, and action icons. This improves readability and dark-mode compatibility while retaining fallback colors.
0.11.10 Adds addPlayerToGroup commands for Sonos group and player drivers. Resolves identifiers by RINCON ID, name, MAC, IP, or device network ID, validates household and group state, and mutates only the requested membership. Includes coverage for forwarding, resolution, ambiguity, inactive groups, and standalone coordinators.
0.11.9 Redesigned the Sonos management UI, made the new interface the default, and improved player discovery and the group editor. Group operations now validate targets and handle eviction without unintended regrouping. Improved favorite loading, playlist playback, WebSocket subscription recovery, and grouped volume updates. Also includes player state, null-safety, and compilation fixes.
0.11.8 Redesigned the Sonos management UI, made the new interface the default, and improved player discovery and the group editor. Group operations now validate targets and handle eviction without unintended regrouping. Improved favorite loading, playlist playback, WebSocket subscription recovery, and grouped volume updates. Also includes player state, null-safety, and compilation fixes.
